title: The Three-Dimensional Structure of Cassiopeia A

evidence.locator: Sect. II.3: every place of the binned Spitzer IRS cubes with a line detected above 3 sigma is fitted with Gaussians; effective resolution 3.7 arcsec for [Ar II] and 10.2 arcsec for [Si II]; velocity resolution 2500 to 3000 km/s. Sect. III: [Ar II] velocities range from about -4000 to 6000 km/s, offset toward positive velocities. Sect. IV.1: the [Ar II] regions fit one spherical shell, 1000 to 2000 km/s thick; v_c = 859 ± 100 km/s, v_m = -4077 ± 200 km/s, S = 0.022 ± 0.002 arcsec per km/s; the infrared ejecta are effectively in free expansion; the forward shock is at a radius of 153 arcsec, and no assertion is made of its offset from the Bright Ring along the velocity axis. Sect. I: the forward shock is a thin ring of X-ray filaments approximately 300 arcsec in diameter (Gotthelf et al. 2001). Sect. IV.1 (3D): the data are smoothed with a 3D Gaussian, the symbol size about 6 arcsec for [Ar II]. Sect. IV.2: the neutron star is placed at 23h 23m 27.94s, +58° 48' 42.5" and zero velocity; the reverse shock's centre is shifted into the sky by 859 km/s, 0.31 pc at a distance of 3.4 kpc.
